# The ages of American comics

Historians often divide American superhero comics into ages.

The Golden Age ran from the late 1930s to the early 1950s. It began with Superman in 1938 and saw the creation of Batman, Wonder Woman and Captain America.

The Silver Age is usually dated from 1956, when DC introduced a new version of the Flash in Showcase #4. It brought a revival of superheroes and, at Marvel, characters such as the Fantastic Four, Spider-Man and the X-Men.

The Bronze Age, from about 1970 to the mid-1980s, brought darker stories and social issues. It was followed by the Modern Age, marked by works such as Watchmen and The Dark Knight Returns in 1986.
